openings.claim: Keep surname dividers; check the reserved reader's surname at shelving, reconcile household-name discrepancies, and update behind-desk exceptions whenever books move. Keep cart arrivals retrievable without compulsory shelving. Faster, correct pickup remains untested.
openings.discriminator: Address correction should reduce second searches and delays, including during the burst; queue congestion predicts persistent burst delays despite verified addresses. Correct addresses with over 5% exceeding two minutes defeats task qualification.
openings.probe: Trial one evening with the existing clerk performing all handoffs, identities behind the desk, two shelves and one cart. Use existing paper, pencils and timing sheet. Cap daily preparation at ten clerk-minutes; stop and record failure if insufficient. Record preparation, reconciliation, second searches, queue presence, arrival-to-handoff time and identity failures; compare burst versus quieter encounters.
openings.uncertainty: Reserved-reader identity access and adequate claimant verification are unconfirmed. Maintaining move-time corrections during service may exceed clerk capacity; eight preparation minutes plus six later correction minutes do not establish feasibility. Bounded resource fit does not prove throughput or correctness.

openings.claim: Existing-cart retrieval may outperform alphabetic shelving; ten sub-minute cart pickups challenge universal shelving superiority.
openings.discriminator: Comparable cart cohorts should remain faster; disappearance with larger arrival volumes or books supports sample selection. Slower retrieval, incorrect handoffs or inadequate capacity defeats routine retention.
openings.probe: Observe naturally occurring cart and shelf pickups using existing resources; record arrival volume, book size and correctness. Keep identities behind the desk, existing-clerk handoffs and ten-minute preparation cap. Treat unmatched comparisons as inconclusive.
openings.uncertainty: Observation fit only: comparable cohorts, capacity and routine-retention performance are unknown.
